dictations.encounter: 71-year-old woman admitted overnight after passing out at home. She takes apixaban. Troponin negative twice. A1c 6.1. Orthostatic vitals positive, BP dropped from 132 to 104 standing. Rule out PE, a CT angiogram of the chest is ordered. Feels lightheaded when she stands quickly. No head injury. Telemetry overnight without events. Echo is pending. Give a 1 liter normal saline bolus and repeat orthostatics this afternoon.

note:
Chief Complaint

Syncope

History of Present Illness

Patient is a 71-year-old woman who presented after passing out at home overnight. She reports feeling lightheaded when she stands quickly. On examination, orthostatic vitals are positive with blood pressure dropping from 132 mmHg to 104 mmHg upon standing. Telemetry overnight was without events. Troponin has been negative on two occasions. Hemoglobin A1c is 6.1. Evaluation for pulmonary embolism is underway with a CT angiogram of the chest ordered. Echocardiography is pending.

Past Medical History

Not provided

Medications

Apixaban — dose not specified in dictation

Allergies

Not provided

Social History

Not provided

Family History

Not provided

Review of Systems

Not documented in today's dictation

Physical Examination

Vital Signs: Orthostatic vitals positive, blood pressure dropped from 132 mmHg to 104 mmHg upon standing.

General: No head injury.

Testing Results

Troponin: negative on two occasions.

Hemoglobin A1c: 6.1.

Imaging: CT angiogram of the chest ordered. Echocardiography pending.

Assessment

Patient is a 71-year-old woman who presented with syncope at home and is found to have orthostatic hypotension. She has negative cardiac biomarkers and is on apixaban. The clinical picture is most consistent with orthostatic syncope, though pulmonary embolism remains on the differential and is being evaluated with CT angiography. Echocardiography is pending to assess for structural cardiac disease. Management will focus on volume repletion and monitoring.

Plan

1. Administer 1 liter normal saline bolus for volume repletion.
2. Repeat orthostatic vital signs this afternoon.
3. Obtain CT angiogram of the chest to rule out pulmonary embolism.
4. Obtain transthoracic echocardiogram when available.
5. Continue apixaban.
6. Continue telemetry monitoring.
